subject.title: [Feature]: Store configuration backup files in their own directory, with datetime name convention

question: Should core config backups move to a dedicated `config-backup/` directory with datetime names, or should OpenClaw keep adjacent backups and only change naming or documentation?
rationale: The source change is feasible, but config backup layout affects upgrade behavior, recovery, retention, diagnostics, and sensitive backup copies, so maintainer product intent is needed before an automated repair is safe.

options.title: Adopt dedicated directory layout
options.body: Make this issue the canonical design and require a migration-safe implementation covering legacy `.bak.N` files, recovery, permissions, retention, audit text, doctor docs, and tests.

options.title: Limit scope to timestamp suffixes
options.body: Keep backups adjacent and route naming-only work through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39923 and its linked PR, while narrowing or rejecting the directory request.

options.title: Keep the current ring
options.body: Reject the layout change for now and document the adjacent numbered backup ring as the intended stable behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt dedicated directory layout
recommendation.body: Make this issue the canonical design and require a migration-safe implementation covering legacy `.bak.N` files, recovery, permissions, retention, audit text, doctor docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history and review context across the config backup, recovery, and test surfaces.
